summary: Leland/Midway off-road racing series beginning with Ivan 'Ironman' Stewart's Super Off Road, then moving into Baja and 3D arcade follow-ups.

entries.title: Ivan 'Ironman' Stewart's Super Off Road
entries.definitive_edition: Arcade Track Pak / Midway Arcade Treasures 3

emulation.notes: Use the arcade game plus Track Pak for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade-accurate output with Track Pak content

primary.version: Arcade release with Track Pak content
primary.why: Super Off Road began as a 1989 arcade game and received many home ports. The arcade route has the original multiplayer cabinet design, and the Track Pak add-on adds eight tracks plus a dune-buggy option; later compilations include both the arcade game and Track Pak.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version and Track Pak through Midway Arcade Treasures 3 if owned, or use original arcade hardware/MAME where legally configured.

entries.remaster_caveats: Some ports omit Ivan Stewart branding because of licensing; the announced Atari Jaguar port was not released.

entries.title: Super Off Road: The Baja

emulation.notes: Use accurate SNES emulation for the primary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Accurate SNES output with modern scaling

primary.why: Super Off Road: The Baja was released for Super NES as a home sequel based on the Baja 1000, changing the series from overhead racing to a third-person camera. The planned Mega Drive version was not released.
primary.how_to_play: Play the SNES version in bsnes, Mesen, MiSTer, or original hardware.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mega Drive/Genesis version was planned but not released.

entries.title: Off Road Challenge

emulation.notes: Use arcade route first, then N64 emulation for the exclusive content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade V Unit output plus N64 supplemental content

primary.version: Original Midway V Unit arcade release
primary.why: Off Road Challenge was first released for arcades on Midway V Unit hardware, with linked cabinet multiplayer and the highest-fidelity original presentation. The Nintendo 64 port adds unlockable tracks and circuit mode, so those extras are a secondary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in supported arcade emulation or original hardware; then use the Nintendo 64 version for its unlockable tracks and circuit mode if desired.

secondary.exclusive_content: Unlockable tracks and an added circuit mode in the Nintendo 64 conversion.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the N64-only circuit mode and unlockable tracks after the arcade primary.
secondary.why: The arcade version is the fidelity route, but the N64 conversion has sourced extra content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster; Nintendo 64 is a content supplement rather than the main route.
